Sections

  • Title, Authors, and Affiliations: PacBio, Resolution of the D4Z4 repeat responsible for facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy with HiFi sequencing. Authors: Zarek Konkel, Joseph M. Dwyer, Jessica Neys, April S. Bartholomew, Shamia Yusuff, Solomon Lynch, Keith Eberle, Z. G. Pecile, Melina A. Kazanidis, Michael A. Eberle. Affiliations include PacBio, Penn GSE, and others.

  • Introduction/Background: The D4Z4 repeat is a variable number tandem repeat (VNTR) that contains some of the most difficult-to-resolve regions in the human genome. D4Z4 has a repeat unit of 3.3 kb encoding the DUX4 protein, implicated in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD). This research aims to understand D4Z4 through a computational approach and aims to produce a thorough resolution of D4Z4 using PacBio HiFi whole-genome sequencing.

  • Methods/Methodology: KiTwi identifies unique haplotypes from individuals with different D4Z4 copy numbers, including 473 population samples from five ancestral populations.

  • Results: Various figures present distribution, methylation levels, and sequence variation of D4Z4 repeats among individuals and populations, confirming the relationship with FSHD.

  • Discussion/Conclusions: The findings suggest the potential for targeted HiFi sequencing methods to further understand and resolve complex genomic regions.

  • References: Lawrence M. et al. “A family-genome model for facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy.” BMJ 2004.

  • Supplementary Text, Acknowledgments, or Footnotes: None noted.

Impact

The poster addresses significant gaps in understanding the genetic basis of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy through advanced sequencing techniques.

Limitations

The poster does not specify the precise caveats of the methodology or the breadth of population diversity explored.

Main Takeaway

The use of HiFi sequencing provides a more accurate and nuanced understanding of D4Z4 in relation to muscular dystrophy.

Keywords

D4Z4, FSHD, HiFi sequencing, haplotypes, genomic resolution, tandem repeat.

Resolution of the D4Z4 repeat responsible for facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy with HiFi sequencing
Zarek Konkel, Joseph M. Dwyer, Jessica Neys, April S. Bartholomew, Shamia Yusuff, Solomon Lynch, Keith Eberle, Z. G. Pecile, Melina A. Kazanidis, Michael A. Eberle
- PacBio, Penn GSE, USA

Introduction
The D4Z4 repeat is a variable number tandem repeat (VNTR) that contains some of the most difficult-to-resolve regions in the human genome. D4Z4 has a repeat unit of 3.3 kb encoding the DUX4 protein, implicated in facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD). This research aims to understand D4Z4 through a computational approach and aims to produce a thorough resolution of D4Z4 using PacBio HiFi whole-genome sequencing.

Application of KiTwi in FSHD Patient Samples
1. 11 FSHD1 samples, allele size known for normal/FSHD patients.
2. 5 samples with SHG/WT variants.
3. 6 samples with normal/SHG/WT.
4. 473 population samples across five ancestral populations.

Kiwvi Workflow
Kiwvi identifies unique haplotypes from individuals with different D4Z4 copy numbers.

Results
- Figure 1: Overview of the D4Z4 focus.

- Figure 3: Repeat and methylation level of all D4Z4 samples.
- Figure 4: Proportions of distal haplotypes on chr4 and chr10.

Discussion
The findings suggest potential for targeted HiFi sequencing methodologies to elucidate D4Z4's complexities.
